pr_title: Quiet grpc info logs in apiserver
pr_body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind cleanup

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Quiets noisy info-level logs in API server by default

Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/98720

alternative to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84061

```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: apiserver making unnecessary log rows
issue_context.body:
**What happened**: we are running apiserver with loglevel 1. However, we are seeing still quite much logs coming from apiserver. ~1800 rows/hour in empty cluster (3 masters, so one apiserver making ~600 rows/hour)

Example:

**What you expected to happen**: I expect that if we run apiserver with loglevel 1 we should only see log rows that we are interested of and are important. As I see it, these log rows are not really important and should not be visible.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**: put apiserver to loglevel 1 and check the log files after that.

comments: Any update on this? This makes debugging more painful. There's a *lot* of noise. cc @thockin.

@BenTheElder the problem is that these log rows are not coming from this repository. Instead these are coming from vendor/google.golang.org/grpc

for instance 
```
I0203 10:15:35.434266       1 clientconn.go:948] ClientConn switching balancer to "pick_first"
```

is coming from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.20.2/vendor/google.golang.org/grpc/clientconn.go#L674

https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc/grpclog#Infof ... which means that it does not matter what loglevel that lib has, it will be always printed still.

they have changed logging stuff in latest grpc-go https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go/blob/master/clientconn.go#L707 and there are some new env variables https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go#how-to-turn-on-logging but no idea can those still be ignored. perhaps not
I don't think GRPC logs klog style lines on its own?, wherever we have the logging adapter we could handle this on our end.
Our shim should probably map GCPC info => V(N) for some N > 1.
I found similar issue with PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/84061 I think it could solve this issue also.

still an issue after update to etcd 3.5.0 and latest grpc in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/100488
@gyuho @ptabor is there a recommended way to quiet the etcd client logs with the new logging setup in 3.5.0?

@liggitt @serathius 
Do you understand the source of this logs ? 

From the high-level glance they might be a syndrome / optimization opportunity: 

1. etcd-3.5. configures clientv3 to use 'roundrobin' balancer by default: 
  https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/76df94a8399eafb48eb8a02d6b1b90868d6b4277/client/v3/internal/resolver/resolver.go#L43
    is it aware decision of api-server to override it to 'pick_first' ? Or the logs are from pre-3.4 and the 3.5 spams with different messages ? 

2. I assume each of this log-lines is somewhat related to creation of clientv3 object instances (or at least connection management within each client, that do not share the connections pool). Taking in consideration that mTLS shandhake on connection is computationally costly, there might be an area for perf improvement.

review_comments:
how do we decide on these levels anymore?
we run kind at 4 in CI I think, so this neatly avoids these, but I think 4 was semi-arbitrary (At best maybe copying kube-up test-config?)
I don't have a very satisfying answer, other than V(5) is the level at which kube-apiserver starts spitting out so much debug info you must not care about log volume
you could also use vmodule to increase verbosity just for this file if you wanted to output these without drowning in other logs
